products: Strategic Role: India's corporate processing and maritime export gateway for raw cotton. Saurashtra handles raw trading, while Kadi (Mehsana district) houses one of the highest concentrations of modern automated double-roller ginning and cottonseed oil expelling units globally.
catchment: Catchment Areas: Rajkot, Amreli, Bhavnagar, Surendranagar, Morbi, Botad, Mehsana, Patan, and interstate inflows from southern Rajasthan and northern Maharashtra.

paragraphs.text: Strategic Role: India's corporate processing and maritime export gateway for raw cotton. Saurashtra handles raw trading, while Kadi (Mehsana district) houses one of the highest concentrations of modern automated double-roller ginning and cottonseed oil expelling units globally.

Key Facilities: High-throughput double-roller (DR) ginning lines, pneumatic lint cleaners, automated moisture restoration towers, and direct container stuffing yards connected to Mundra and Pipavav ports.
Catchment Areas: Rajkot, Amreli, Bhavnagar, Surendranagar, Morbi, Botad, Mehsana, Patan, and interstate inflows from southern Rajasthan and northern Maharashtra.

passages.text: Saurashtra Peninsula (Rajkot, Amreli, Bhavnagar, Surendranagar & Morbi) (~65% – 72% of state output):
North Gujarat (Kadi, Mehsana, Patan & Sabarkantha) (~16% – 20% of state output):
Remaining Districts (~4% – 7%): Ahmedabad rural, Kutch, and Dahod.

Maharashtra commands the largest physical area under cotton in India (>4.2 million hectares), but per-hectare productivity remains below the national average (~320–360 kg lint/ha) due to heavy reliance on monsoon rainfall (>95% rainfed) across the Deccan plateau.
Vidarbha Belt (Yavatmal, Amravati, Akola, Wardha & Nagpur) (~52% – 58% of state output):
Marathwada Belt (Jalna, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Nanded & Parbhani) (~26% – 30% of state output):
Khandesh Belt (Jalgaon, Dhule & Nandurbar) (~14% – 18% of state output):
Remaining Districts (~4% – 6%): Beed, Buldhana, and Ahmednagar.
Northern & Eastern Godavari Basin (Adilabad, Komaram Bheem Asifabad & Nirmal) (~34% – 38% of state output):
Warangal, Hanumakonda, Jangaon & Mahabubabad (~28% – 32% of state output):
Remaining Districts (~12% – 16%): Karimnagar, Nagarkurnool, and Sangareddy.

Northern Rajasthan (Ganganagar and Hanumangarh) accounts for >70% of state volume. Sown in April–May under the Indira Gandhi Canal (IGNP) and Bhakra canal systems, recording some of the highest lint productivities in the country (>650–700 kg/ha).
Sirsa alone accounts for over 40% of Haryana's cotton output. The region is heavily mechanized, hosting modern high-speed ginning facilities.

Home to Suvin, the finest commercial extra-long staple (ELS) cotton variety in the world (spinning up to 240s count, rivaling Egyptian Giza and American Pima). Though a minor producer of lint, Tamil Nadu houses over 45% to 50% of India's total spinning mill spindle capacity, importing raw bales continuously from Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Telangana.

protection.geography: All-India Commercial Belts (Heavy in Central & Southern zones)
protection.impact: Larvae burrow into flower buds, webbing petals into a characteristic "Rosette Flower"; larvae bore into young green bolls, feeding internally on seeds and severing fibers; causes locule rot, immature boll opening, and yellow-stained lint; widespread field resistance to Bt Cry1Ac/Cry2Ab toxins.

protection.name: Cotton Leaf Curl Virus (CLCuV) (Geminivirus transmitted by Whitefly Bemisia tabaci)
protection.geography: Northern Irrigated Belt (Severe in Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan)
protection.impact: Upward/downward curling of leaf margins; thickening of veins on the leaf underside; formation of leafy enations (cup-like green outgrowths) on the veins of lower leaf surfaces; severe stunting and reduction in boll number; causes 20–80% yield collapse.
protection.passage: Cotton — source table 138, row 3. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Sucking Pest Complex: Jassids & Thrips (Amrasca biguttula, Thrips tabaci)
protection.impact:
Jassids: Nymphs and adults suck sap from leaf undersides, injecting toxic saliva; margins turn yellow, curl down, turn brick-red, and dry up ("Hopper Burn").

Thrips: Lacerate leaf surfaces, causing silvering, crinkling, and upward cupping of leaves.
protection.passage: Cotton — source table 138, row 4. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Bacterial Leaf Blight / Angular Leaf Spot (Xanthomonas citri pv. malvacearum)
protection.geography: High-Humidity Monsoon Belts (Heavy in Vertisols of Central/South)
protection.impact: Four distinct field symptoms: (1) Angular, water-soaked brown spots bounded by leaf veins on foliage; (2) Black, elongated cankers along veins and branches ("Black Arm"); (3) Circular sunken water-soaked spots on bolls; (4) Seedling blight.
protection.passage: Cotton — source table 138, row 5. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Grey Mildew / "Dahiya" Disease (Ramularia areola)
protection.impact: Angular, pale-white to translucent spots appear on leaf undersides, covered by a frosty white powdery growth of conidiophores; leaves turn yellow, become necrotic, and drop prematurely (severe defoliation); suppresses late boll filling.
protection.passage: Cotton — source table 138, row 6. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Boll Rot Complex & Fire Hazards (Fusarium, Colletotrichum, Aspergillus)
protection.impact: Moisture ingress in raw seed cotton (Kapas) causes fungal rotting and brownish-grey fiber discoloration inside unopened bolls; friction in drying cylinders and static in pneumatics can ignite dry lint.
protection.passage: Cotton — source table 138, row 7. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.
